title: Integral internal Hom and reduction
statement:
Fix the integral coefficient datum of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]: a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t=\varpi_E$, and a scheme $X$. On the small pro-etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $B=R_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/t^n)_X$, $A_n=R/t^n$, and $B_n=(A_n)_X$. Write $D(B)$ and $D(B_n)$ for the unbounded derived categories of module sheaves. Let $F_n=-\otimes_B^L B_n:D(B)\to D(B_n)$ be derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] and let $U_n=\operatorname{Res}_n:D(B_n)\to D(B)$ be derived restriction of scalars [def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars]. Internal Hom is the ambient ringed-site derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], denoted $H_B$ and $H_{B_n}$.

For arbitrary $K,L\in D(B)$ and every integer $n\geq1$, set $K_n=F_nK$ and $L_n=F_nL$. The canonical map
$$
 c_{n,K,L}:F_nH_B(K,L)\longrightarrow H_{B_n}(K_n,L_n)
$$
is an isomorphism in $D(B_n)$. Here $c_{n,K,L}$ is the transpose of the pairing
$$
 F_nK\otimes_{B_n}^LF_nH_B(K,L)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}F_n(K\otimes_B^LH_B(K,L))
 \xrightarrow{F_n(\operatorname{ev}_{K,L})}F_nL.
$$
Thus the comparison preserves evaluation and its transposes under tensor-Hom adjunction. If $L$ is derived complete in the sense of [def-weil-derived-complete], then $H_B(K,L)$ is derived complete. No boundedness, constructibility or site-perfectness assumption on $K$ or $L$ is imposed in the comparison, and completeness of $K$ is not required.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $R=\mathcal O_E$ is a principal ideal domain. Every ideal is therefore generated by one element, so $R$ is Noetherian, as required by the completion lemma below. Use the coefficient resolution $[R\xrightarrow{t^n}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect]. By [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction], its constant sheaf resolution tensored with $B$ resolves $B_n$ through the canonical projection $B\to B_n$. Consequently $Q_n=[B\xrightarrow{t^n}B]$ represents $U_nB_n$. Its terms are free, hence flat (tensoring with $B$ is the identity), and it is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. For $m\geq n$, the chain map $Q_m\to Q_n$ has components $(t^{m-n},1)$ in degrees $(-1,0)$: $t^nt^{m-n}=t^m$. It lifts $B_m\to B_n$, composes correctly, and carries the degree-zero map $B[0]\to Q_m$ to $B[0]\to Q_n$. All resolutions here are over $B$, not over a larger finite quotient.

source.place: Tag 093M, sites-modules-lemma-completion-flat; Tag 06YQ, sites-cohomology-lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; the principal regular-element resolution

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ for the chosen small site. For either coefficient sheaf $C=B$ or $B_n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and then [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] to obtain the natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(C)}(T,H_C(K,N))
 \cong H^0(\mathcal C,H_C(T,H_C(K,N)))
 \cong H^0(\mathcal C,H_C(T\otimes_C^LK,N))
 \cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(C)}(T\otimes_C^LK,N).$$
Here $H^0(\mathcal C,-)$ is global hypercohomology as defined in the second cited node; it is a group, whereas degree-zero cohomology of the internal Hom alone is a sheaf. The counit is evaluation $H_C(K,N)\otimes_C^LK\to N$; composing with the tensor symmetry gives the convention $K\otimes_C^LH_C(K,N)\to N$ in the statement. In particular $H_C(K,-)$ is right adjoint to $-\otimes_C^LK$ on the ambient unbounded category. The tensor reassociations and symmetry used below can be checked on flat-term K-flat representatives and descend by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]: reassociation sends $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$ to $x\otimes(y\otimes z)$, and symmetry sends $x\otimes y$ to $(-1)^{|x||y|}y\otimes x$. The differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] shows both are chain maps; their inverse formulas and their coherence follow on pure tensors.

proof.text:
Regard the identity of the topos with coefficient map $B\to B_n$ as a morphism of ringed topoi. The canonical adjunction in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] gives $F_n\dashv U_n$: its right derived direct image is precisely $U_n$, since restriction is exact and is applied termwise as in [def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars]. The tensor isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives
$$F_n(T\otimes_B^LK)\cong F_nT\otimes_{B_n}^LF_nK.$$
It is the usual tensor associativity map on K-flat resolutions. Thus the pairing in the statement has the indicated source and target, and Step 2 defines its transpose $c_{n,K,L}$. Restriction $U_n$ is conservative: it leaves the underlying sheaf complex unchanged and commutes with cohomology; the cone of a morphism whose restriction is an isomorphism has zero underlying cohomology and hence zero $B_n$-module cohomology.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), and 015F (derived exact restriction); conservativity by cohomology and the cone criterion

proof.text:
For $N\in D(B_n)$ and every $T\in D(B)$, the adjunctions of Steps 2 and 3 and the tensor comparison give natural bijections
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_B(T,U_nH_{B_n}(F_nK,N))
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{B_n}(F_nT,H_{B_n}(F_nK,N))\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{B_n}(F_nT\otimes_{B_n}^LF_nK,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{B_n}(F_n(T\otimes_B^LK),N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(T\otimes_B^LK,U_nN)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(T,H_B(K,U_nN)).
\end{aligned}$$
The generic fully faithful Yoneda statement [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful], applied to $D(B)$, turns this natural isomorphism of represented functors into an isomorphism $e_{K,N}:U_nH_{B_n}(F_nK,N)\cong H_B(K,U_nN)$. The inverse is the image of the identity under the inverse bijections; naturality makes the composites identities. This is an internal-Hom restriction comparison, not an assertion that $U_n$ is fully faithful. In particular it applies to $N=F_nL$ with no perfectness condition on $K$.

source.place: Tags 08J9, 08JA, 07A6, 07A4; generic Yoneda applied to the displayed natural Hom bijections

proof.text:
We now prove invertibility of the specific $B$-linear tensor-Hom map
$$d_n:H_B(K,L)\otimes_B^LB_n\longrightarrow H_B(K,U_nF_nL),$$
the transpose of evaluation tensored with $B_n$. Choose a K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and a K-injective representative $I$ of $L$ as in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Use the K-flat resolution $Q_n$ from Step 1 to compute tensor with $B_n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-split-perfect-tensor-kinjective], $\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes_BQ_n)$ is K-injective: $Q_n$ is bounded, and its two nonzero terms are $B$, with the identity splitting into $B^1$ (the other terms are zero). Thus the two sides of $d_n$ are represented by
$$\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)\otimes_BQ_n
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes_BQ_n)).$$
Here tensor with $Q_n$ computes derived tensor for any complex; in particular no boundedness of $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)$ or of $P$ was used.

source.place: Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), Section 08J7 (internal Hom construction), Tag 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective), specialized to the dual of the bounded free complex Q_n

proof.text:
The actual map between the complexes in Step 5 sends a homogeneous $f$ of Hom degree $a$ and $q\in Q_n^b$ to the map
$$x\longmapsto(-1)^{b|x|}f(x)\otimes q.$$
This follows by transposing evaluation and using the tensor symmetry of Step 2. In total degree $a+b$, the differential formulas in [def-pur-hom-complex] and [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] agree: the contributions involving $d_I,d_P,d_Q$ have respectively signs $(-1)^{bp}$, $(-1)^{a+1+bp}$, $(-1)^{a+bp+p}$ on $x\in P^p$ on both sides. For $b=0,-1$ the terms $Q_n^b=B$ are rank one, so this map is a degreewise isomorphism: a pair of families of maps is the same as a family of pairs, and its inverse reverses the two identifications with the same signs. This remains true for unbounded $P$, since only the two coefficient degrees are interchanged with the product over $p$. Hence $d_n$ is an isomorphism. The formula is natural in chain maps of $Q_n$, including the maps $(t^{m-n},1)$ and $B[0]\to Q_n$ from Step 1; the latter sends $f$ to $f\otimes1$.

source.place: Section 0A8X (Hom complex differential) and total tensor of Section 06YL; explicit signed evaluation calculation

proof.text:
Under the isomorphism $U_nF_nH_B(K,L)=H_B(K,L)\otimes_B^LB_n$ and $e_{K,F_nL}$ of Step 4, $U_n(c_{n,K,L})$ equals $d_n$. Indeed the Hom bijections in Step 4 carry $U_n(c_{n,K,L})$ to exactly the pairing obtained by $F_n$ from evaluation; its transpose back over $B$ is evaluation tensored with $B_n$, which is the map computed in Steps 5 and 6. The units and counits are the canonical ones of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]; no isomorphism between unspecified cones is being chosen. Since $e_{K,F_nL}$ and $d_n$ are isomorphisms, $U_n(c_{n,K,L})$ is an isomorphism, and conservativity from Step 3 proves the claim in $D(B_n)$.

For evaluation compatibility, by construction
$$\operatorname{ev}_{K_n,L_n}\circ(1\otimes c_{n,K,L})
=F_n(\operatorname{ev}_{K,L})\circ\mu^{-1},$$
where $\mu:F_n(K\otimes_B^LH_B(K,L))\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nK\otimes_{B_n}^LF_nH_B(K,L)$ is the tensor comparison. If $a:T\to H_B(K,L)$ transposes to $f:T\otimes_B^LK\to L$, naturality of $\mu$ and this equality show that $c_{n,K,L}\circ F_na$ transposes to $F_nf$ under $F_nT\otimes_{B_n}^LF_nK\cong F_n(T\otimes_B^LK)$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves compatibility with every such transpose.

proof.text:
Suppose $L$ is derived complete. By [def-weil-derived-complete], writing $M_n=U_nF_nL$ and $v_n:M_{n+1}\to M_n$ for the reduction transitions, its actual reduction maps $u_n:L\to M_n$ are the first components of a Roos triangle
$$L\longrightarrow\prod_nM_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nM_n\longrightarrow L[1],
\qquad \pi_ns=v_n\pi_{n+1}.$$
These countable products exist: [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] applies to the sheaf of rings $B$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and clause 2 of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] supplies the derived products. Put $H=H_B(K,-)$. By Step 2 this is a right adjoint, so [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits], applied to the discrete category of positive integers, gives an isomorphism
$$\rho:H(\prod_nM_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_nH(M_n),\qquad \pi'_n\rho=H(\pi_n).$$
It preserves distinguished triangles and shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], and is additive. If $s'$ is the endomorphism of $\prod_nH(M_n)$ with components $\pi'_ns'=H(v_n)\pi'_{n+1}$, functoriality gives
$$\pi'_n\rho H(s)=H(\pi_ns)=H(v_n)H(\pi_{n+1})=\pi'_ns'\rho.$$
Equality of all product projections proves $\rho H(s)=s'\rho$; additivity then gives $\rho H(1-s)=(1-s')\rho$. The first map has components $H(u_n)$ by the same projection identity. Thus applying $H$ and these product identifications gives a distinguished triangle with the actual transition endomorphism $1-s'$.

The isomorphisms $d_n$ of Steps 5 and 6 identify this tower with the reductions $U_nF_nH_B(K,L)$. They identify $H_B(K,u_n)$ with the actual reduction map of $H_B(K,L)$: on the coefficient models this is precisely $f\mapsto f\otimes1$, and the transitions are the explicit chain maps $(t^{m-n},1)$. Thus the transported triangle is the Roos triangle required by [def-weil-derived-complete] for $H_B(K,L)$. This proves completeness without a perfectness or completeness hypothesis on $K$.

split_report.summary: Made the previously unbound coefficient notation and categories explicit, preserving all clauses. Expanded the finite-free coefficient argument to a signed chain isomorphism, constructed the internal coefficient-adjunction comparison via Hom bijections, identified the evaluation-defined map, and proved completeness by applying the actual right adjoint to the Roos triangle. Reused existing nodes; no new nodes. The small-etale Lean declarations do not attach the full pro-etale statement, and the full comparison there still has sorry. Rebased against live DAG tip a80ba567c0686df5898bb0fe646344706177b1af and tightened the right-adjoint limit step after re-reading changed dependency statements. Second reader corrected Step 2 to use global hypercohomology, distinguished the two evaluation orders, and replaced the Step 8 tower/product claim by projection equations for 1-s; the original blueprint and Stacks sources were recovered and read in the launcher literature copy. Cited the existing DVR theorem explicitly to verify the completion lemma’s Noetherian hypothesis; the final proof uses twenty-one existing dependencies.
